parameters.content:
## Sheet Poller
Watches the "Jobs" tab of the Google Sheet in Client Config (jobsSheetId) for rows with Status = "Complete", and fires each one through the already-tested main workflow's own webhook - reusing all of its validation/Xero/email logic rather than duplicating any of it.

Three ways this runs:
- Schedule Trigger: real production path, every 5 minutes.
- Manual Trigger: editor testing.
- Webhook (POST /webhook/invoice/poll-now): on-demand / API testing, same pattern used everywhere else in this template.

After each row is processed, its Status cell is written back ("Invoiced" / "Skipped - Duplicate" / "Error - ...") so it's never reprocessed on the next poll, plus invoiceReference/invoiceNumber/processedAt/errorMessage for traceability. Only rows whose Status is literally "Complete" (case-sensitive) are picked up - staff should leave Status blank until a job is genuinely done.

Uses raw Google Sheets REST API calls (HTTP Request nodes) rather than the native Google Sheets node - that node's column-mapping/resourceMapper behavior proved unreliable in live testing (a Read/Update combination either errored outright or silently wrote unrelated webhook-request fields into the sheet). The raw REST pattern here is the same proven-working approach already used for Xero throughout this project.

See workflows/invoice-automation/README.md for the exact Jobs tab column layout this expects.

nodes.name: Process Complete Rows
nodes.notes: Calls the main workflow's own already-tested webhook per qualifying row, sequentially (awaited one at a time - deliberately not parallel, to avoid concurrent Xero calls racing). Builds a Sheets values.update range (columns I-M: status, invoiceReference, invoiceNumber, processedAt, errorMessage) per row for the next node. Row I..M assumes the exact Jobs tab column order from the README - if that ever changes, update the column letters here.

nodes.name: Update Row
nodes.notes: One PUT per qualifying row (n8n's default per-item HTTP Request behavior) - fine at the expected small volume of jobs per poll. alwaysOutputData: true so a poll with zero qualifying rows still reaches Build Poll Summary instead of silently producing no output (same zero-items gotcha found earlier in the phone booking build).

parameters.jsCode:
const processed = $('Process Complete Rows').all().map(i => i.json).filter(r => r.updateRange);
return [{ json: { rowsProcessed: processed.length, results: processed } }];
